expected.rationale: Diagnostic, not a required reject: the prior independent evaluation penalized contradictory uncertainty/generalization wording. The Verdict passage actually documents the shared weave.init project argument, so an integration-page origin alone is not evidence of unsupported applicability. Preserve the new judgment and reasons without requiring either verdict.

claims.text: Pass a string in the form "<your-team>/<your-project>": CoreWeave Forge team name and W&B project name.
claims.answer_quote: Pass a string in the form `"<your-team>/<your-project>"`: your CoreWeave Forge team name and your Weights & Biases project name [S2].

claims.text: It registers team and project with Weave; SDK uses this to route spans.
claims.answer_quote: It registers your team and project with Weave. The SDK uses this to send spans to the right place in the UI [S4].

claims.text: In the quickstart it authenticates with W&B and configures the OTel exporter.
claims.answer_quote: it authenticates with Weights & Biases and configures the OpenTelemetry (OTel) exporter that sends agent spans to the **Agents** view [S1].

claims.text: Project is created on first write if missing.
claims.answer_quote: If the project doesn't exist on your team yet, Weave creates it the first time you write to it [S1].
It returns a client. The getting-started example assigns it with `client = weave.init(...)` [S2].
claims.scope_reason: S2 only shows assignment to client, not documented return semantics; though the second sentence is accurate, 'returns a client' is an inference.

claims.text: Call before start_* functions; they silently no-op if init is absent.
claims.answer_quote: Those functions silently do nothing if the init call is absent [S4].

claims.text: A project name alone logs to default team/entity; treated as general behavior of weave.init.
claims.answer_quote: I'm treating it as general behavior of `weave.init`.
claims.scope_reason: S3 documents this for the Verdict integration; generalization is explicitly unconfirmed and not supported.

claims.answer_quote: The quickstart sets the `WANDB_API_KEY` environment variable to your CoreWeave Forge API key before calling `weave.init` [S1].

issues: The claim that weave.init returns a client is inferred only from an assignment example; qualify it or remove it.
